title: Bidirectional motion of antiferromagnetic skyrmions driven by competing spin torques
authors: Laichuan Shen, Wang Kang, Xichao Zhang, Qiuping Huang, Yalin Lu, Zhifeng Zhu, Yan Zhou
abstract: Antiferromagnetic skyrmions are swirling topological spin textures with rich dynamics and intriguing transport properties, yet their bidirectional dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the dynamics of antiferromagnetic skyrmions driven by current-induced spin-transfer and spin-orbit torques. We computationally demonstrate that antiferromagnetic skyrmions moving in one direction at low current densities can reverse their motion direction when the driving current is above a threshold. Based on the Thiele approach analysis, we show that this bidirectional motion originates from a change in the relative strengths of two effective forces arising from spin-transfer and spin-orbit torques. Furthermore, exploiting this bidirectional motion on a single racetrack, we design programmable logic gates. Our results not only uncover a hidden mechanism for bidirectional skyrmion motion but also facilitate the development of antiferromagnet-based logic devices.
summary: This work explores how antiferromagnetic skyrmions exhibit bidirectional motion when subjected to competing spin torques (STT and SOT). By analyzing the force balance governing this motion, the authors demonstrate that a critical current threshold causes the skyrmion direction to reverse. This controllable mechanism is then leveraged to propose and validate programmable logic gates based on magnetic racetrack devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the previously unexplored bidirectional dynamics of antiferromagnetic skyrmions when driven by competing spin-transfer torque (STT) and spin-orbit torque (SOT). The goal is to utilize this mechanism for developing programmable logic devices.
main_result: It was computationally demonstrated that AFM skyrmion motion can reverse direction above a critical current threshold. This bidirectional motion, tunable by an external magnetic field, enables the design of functional logic gates.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using micromagnetic simulations solving the LLG equation and supplemented by the Thiele approach for analytical understanding of the force balance.
model_or_system: The system models antiferromagnetic skyrmions in a structure coupled with a heavy metal layer to induce interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. The dynamics are governed by current-induced STT and SOT forces acting on the topological spin texture.
key_observables: Skyrmion velocity ($v_x$), force components ($F_{STT}, F_{SOT}$), skyrmion radius ($R_s$), and logic gate output states (e.g., AND, OR, XOR).
important_parameters: Driving current density ($j$), out-of-plane magnetic field ($B_z$), and the relative strengths of STT vs. SOT torques.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Thiele equation approximation for describing the collective dynamics, and it assumes that logic operation limits can be controlled by local current modulation factors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate velocity reversal ($v_x$ vs $j$) showing positive to negative changes; force balance plots show sign reversals in net force; and schematics demonstrate AND/OR/XOR gate functionality based on current ranges.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and uses simulations to observe bidirectional motion. It then analyzes the underlying physics using the Thiele equation, showing that the reversal stems from competing torques affecting skyrmion size. Finally, it applies this understanding to design and demonstrate programmable logic gates in a racetrack geometry.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics rather than fundamental quantum information, the study deals with non-equilibrium dynamics of topological textures driven by external currents, which shares conceptual links with open quantum systems modeling where dissipation and driving fields are crucial.
